stem: A client has a significant electrical injury but only small external entry and exit wounds. Which assessment principle is most important?

options.A: The external wounds may underestimate deep tissue and systemic injury, so broader evaluation including cardiac assessment is required
options.B: Small skin wounds prove the electrical injury is minor
options.C: Electrical current causes damage only at the visible entry wound
options.D: Cardiac effects are impossible when external burns are small

rationale: Electrical injuries can cause deep tissue damage and systemic complications that are disproportionate to visible skin injury. Current references emphasize cardiac assessment/monitoring for more than minor low-voltage injuries and evaluation for complications such as muscle injury and rhabdomyolysis.
educational_objective: Recognize that the visible skin injury can underestimate the severity of an electrical injury.
source_claim_supported: Supports deep tissue/systemic injury despite limited external wounds and the need for cardiac monitoring/evaluation when appropriate.
correction_summary: Preserved the source construct while tightening it to the core principle and avoiding an unsupported claim that every electrical exposure requires identical monitoring.
audit_findings: A reflects the known hidden-injury pattern; B-D falsely equate external wound size with internal severity.
